# Results — Study 471 (QQE — Quantitative Qualitative Estimation)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a long
fires when the smoothed RSI crosses above its QQE trailing band: momentum ignition that price
continues** — encoded as a mechanical rule. The QQE line is a Wilder-smoothed RSI (RSI MA); its
fast line is an ATR-of-the-smoothed-RSI trailing stop (factor 4.236) built as a causal dual-band
trailing stop; a long fires on the bar where RSI MA crosses **above** the stop, entered at the
**next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **697** mechanical QQE band-crosses pooled across the 5 tapes (RSI len = 14, smoothing = 5, factor = 4.236) |
| Timing / costs | causal Wilder smoothing (no look-ahead); cross read on close of *t*, enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per cross |

> **Why a *robust* random baseline.** A single random draw of a few hundred entry dates is itself
> noisy — a lucky-low draw can sit ~100 bps below the true drift and manufacture a fake edge for
> the rule. The baseline here is **pooled over 40 random seeds** (~28k entries/horizon), which
> estimates the actual unconditional drift the rule competes against. (With one unlucky seed the
> QQE cross *appears* to beat random at Welch *t* ≈ 3 — that apparent edge is entirely an
> under-estimated baseline, and it vanishes the moment the baseline is estimated properly.)

## The signal — QQE band-cross vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch cross-vs-random** *t* against the robust baseline is the test that matters. Δ = cross − random.

| horizon | n | cross | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (cross−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 696 | +31.5 bps | 59% | +3.72 | +28.8 bps | **+2.8 bps** | +29.5 bps | +0.28 | 0.777 |
| 10-day | 696 | +60.3 bps | 62% | +5.39 | +57.0 bps | **+3.3 bps** | +58.3 bps | +0.25 | 0.802 |
| 20-day | 695 | +100.7 bps | 64% | +7.01 | +110.6 bps | **−9.9 bps** | +98.7 bps | −0.50 | 0.619 |
| 60-day | 690 | +310.2 bps | 70% | +9.05 | +304.1 bps | **+6.0 bps** | +308.2 bps | +0.19 | 0.846 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks spectacular (**+7.01** at 20 days,
**+9.05** at 60) — but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index inherit
the drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the QQE cross is statistically
indistinguishable from buying on random days (Δ = +2.8 / +3.3 / −9.9 / +6.0 bps). The
cross-minus-random difference **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** (max Welch *t* = +0.28 at
5 days, *p* = 0.78). The band-cross does not forecast.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — the cross does not beat random

| ticker | entries | cross | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (cross−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 139 | +103.6 bps | +3.48 | +104.8 bps | **−1.2 bps** |
| QQQ | 142 | +104.5 bps | +2.96 | +150.8 bps | **−46.3 bps** |
| IWM | 140 | +118.9 bps | +2.93 | +101.1 bps | **+17.8 bps** |
| DIA | 136 | +84.0 bps | +3.34 | +92.0 bps | **−8.0 bps** |
| GLD | 140 | +92.1 bps | +2.37 | +103.0 bps | **−10.9 bps** |

Only **IWM** edges out a positive delta (+17.8 bps); in 4 of 5 names the QQE cross matches or
*underperforms* a dart-throwing entry. No coherent cross-sectional edge — the hallmark of
relabelled drift.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the timing, nothing changes

The decisive "does the QQE structure matter?" test: rebuild the band on a **Fourier
phase-randomised surrogate** of the close path — same power spectrum / return marginal, but the
timing of the turning points destroyed. If the band-cross genuinely keyed off real momentum
ignition, the scramble should collapse the result.

| test | observed band-cross 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY phase-scramble | +103.6 bps | **0.313** | 500 |

**31% of phase-scrambled tapes match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.313). The QQE geometry carries
no information beyond the marginal drift — scrambled-timing tapes do nearly as well. "The band-cross
forecasts" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real continuation

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* post-cross continuation (knob `edge`), the same band-cross
rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a
dead detector.

| planted edge | n | cross | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no continuation) | 107 | −64.3 bps | 46% | −1.47 |
| **0.60** (real planted continuation) | 81 | +703.3 bps | 81% | **+9.73** |

With no planted continuation the control sits at *t* < 0 (no false positive); a real planted
continuation lights up at *t* = +9.73 with an 81% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The QQE band-cross does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline
  (cross − random = +2.8 / +3.3 / −9.9 / +6.0 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the cross-vs-random Welch
  *t* never clears 2, max +0.28 at 5 days, *p* = 0.78). The impressive one-sample *t*'s (20-day
  +7.01, 60-day +9.05) are pure beta — the upward drift of long equity indices. **Caveat:** with a
  single unlucky random seed the cross *appears* to win at Welch *t* ≈ 3; that "edge" is an
  under-estimated baseline and evaporates once the baseline is pooled over many seeds.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed, and costs only deepen the hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply and more fully by
  holding the index; the cross rule trades less and pays costs on each signal, dominating nothing.
- **"Does the QQE band-cross forecast"? — BUSTED.** The phase-scramble placebo leaves the result
  intact (*p* = 0.313): scrambled-timing tapes do as well as the real one, so the specific QQE
  geometry carries no forecasting information. QQE is a smoothed re-description of momentum, not a
  forecasting strategy.
